subject: Request to hold collection: midcycle embedding-count anomaly / provisional credit
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@starlend.io>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: billing@starlend.io
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected jump in embed charges — request to pause collection

Hi Jasmine,

We just received our provisional September invoice and noticed a ~4x lift in embedding token counts for API key proj-starlend-main between 2027-09-07 and 2027-09-14. The usage looks like a repeated duplication within batched embedding calls — many 1K-batch requests appear to be double-counted.

Can you please:
- Pause collection on the outstanding invoice while we investigate?
- Provide a CSV snapshot of per-request counts for that key (timestamps + request_id + billed_tokens) for 2027-09-07 -> 2027-09-14?
- Confirm whether any model variant or backend rollout happened during that window that could cause double-counting of paired sequences in the new batching path.

I'm attaching a short sample export from our side (starlend_usage_snapshot_sep2027.csv). We plan to withhold payment until this is reconciled; please advise whether Redwood can issue a provisional credit if root cause looks like a platform-side duplication.

Thanks — this is blocking our finance team for month-end.

—Elena
Elena Ruiz
Head of Data Platform | Starlend
billing@starlend.io
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai

Elena — thanks for the early heads up and for the export. I've looped in Ben (account lead), Lauren (billing), and Markus (infra) to help triage.

Immediate plan:
1) Lauren — can we put a temporary hold on collection for the disputed line items and create a provisional credit while we investigate?
2) Markus / infra — please pull per-request metering logs for proj-starlend-main for 2027-09-07 -> 2027-09-14 (request_id, backend_model, batch_size, billed_tokens, ingest_ts).
3) Ben / Jasmine — we will coordinate a 30-min triage call today after we have the logs.

Elena, we'll review your CSV and get back with the snapshot from our side within 48 hours. Thanks for flagging this early.

—Jasmine
Jasmine Liu

Lauren — can you confirm whether we can suspend the automated dunning flow for Starlend and issue a provisional credit for the disputed period?

Context for billing: the customer is explicitly withholding payment until reconciliation. They have a healthy account and are in good standing; we should avoid escalation. If legal needs a formal credit memo, let me know.

Elena — thank you for the sample. We're prioritizing this — Markus indicated there was a lightweight batching optimization rolled to a subset of accounts on 2027-09-09, but it's not obvious it would double-count. Markus, please advise ASAP.

> Lauren — can you confirm whether we can suspend the automated dunning flow for Starlend and issue a provisional credit for the disputed period?

Ben / Jasmine / Elena — we can put collection on hold for up to 14 days while engineering completes the root-cause. I've created a provisional credit equal to the invoiced delta for 2027-09-07 -> 2027-09-14 (line item: "Embeddings usage - provisional adj") pending final reconciliation. Attached is a provisional invoice PDF (invoice_2027_09_provisional.pdf) reflecting the hold.

To finalize we need:
- Redwood metering snapshot (per-request) for the disputed key (Markus to provide).
- Reconciliation doc from customer (we have Elena's CSV).
- Short triage note summarizing root cause and whether credit should be permanent or reversed.

Lauren Bishop
Revenue Operations Manager | Redwood Inference
From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@starlend.io>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected jump in embed charges — request to pause collection

Jasmine / Ben / Lauren / Elena — attaching the initial metering snapshot we pulled (link below) and a short findings summary.

Summary:
- We rolled a micro-optimization to the embedding batching layer on 2027-09-09 02:10:37 UTC targeted at latency-sensitive tenants. The change altered how paired-sequence batched requests were normalized when a client submitted multi-part sequences in a single batch. For most clients the norming was idempotent; for clients using a legacy batching header (X-Client-Batch-V1), an edge-case caused a double-count increment to billed_tokens when the SDK retried an internal chunk.
- Starlend's telemetry shows repeated CDS-retries from their client at 2027-09-10 04:21 -> 04:35 UTC that line up with the doubled billed_tokens. We see request_ids matching Elena's sample in the attached CSV export.

Action taken:
1) We have reverted the micro-optimization for the affected cohort as of 2027-09-10 05:02 UTC.
2) We exported per-request billed_tokens for proj-starlend-main for 2027-09-07 -> 2027-09-14 and placed the CSV at: https://redwood.app/drive/starlend-telemetry-202709.csv
3) Based on matching request_ids, we recommend a permanent credit for the duplicated tokens during 2027-09-09 -> 2027-09-10 window. Approx provisional credit: $3,420.00.

Elena — sorry for the disruption. We'll proceed with permanent adjustment after you confirm the matching rows in your export. Lauren, please confirm the next step to convert the provisional credit into a final credit memo and reflect it on the account.

--- Attached: starlend_metering_snapshot_202709.csv (link above) ---

Markus Klein
Engineering Lead, Inference Runtime | Redwood Inference
